items.question: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration?
items.explanation: Most of the ATP in a eukaryotic cell is produced in the mitochondria.

items.question: Which structure controls what enters and leaves a cell?
Which organelles are the site of protein synthesis?
What type of cell has no nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles?
items.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes; their DNA lies free in the cytoplasm.

items.question: How many micrometres are there in one millimetre?

items.text: Water moves across a partially permeable membrane by {{osmosis}}.
items.explanation: Water moves from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one.

items.text: The net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration is called {{diffusion}}.
Moving substances against a concentration gradient using energy from ATP is called {{active transport}}.
Plant cell walls are made mainly of {{cellulose}}.
Mitosis produces two {{genetically identical}} daughter nuclei.
items.explanation: Mitosis is used for growth, repair and asexual reproduction.

items.question: What are the monomers of proteins?
Which bond links amino acids in a polypeptide?
items.explanation: It forms in a condensation reaction that releases water.

items.question: What is the region of an enzyme where the substrate binds called?
Which molecule is the main energy currency of the cell?
Which reagent turns blue-black in the presence of starch?
What are the products of aerobic respiration?

items.text: Enzymes speed up reactions by lowering the {{activation energy}}.
At high temperatures an enzyme {{denatures}} and its active site changes shape.
items.explanation: The substrate no longer fits, so the rate of reaction falls.

items.text: Glucose and fructose are examples of {{monosaccharides / monosaccharide}}.
Anaerobic respiration in human muscles produces {{lactate / lactic acid}}.

items.question: What is the shape of a DNA molecule?

Which base replaces thymine in RNA?
How many chromosomes are in a normal human body cell?
What term describes an organism with two different alleles of a gene?
What is a random change in the base sequence of DNA called?

items.text: Different versions of the same gene are called {{alleles / allele}}.
Meiosis produces {{haploid}} gametes with half the number of chromosomes.
Charles Darwin proposed evolution by {{natural selection}}.

items.question: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
Which chamber of the heart pumps blood to the rest of the body?
items.explanation: It has the thickest muscular wall of the four chambers.

items.question: Which hormone lowers blood glucose concentration?
Which organ produces insulin?
Which white blood cells produce antibodies?

items.text: Gas exchange in the lungs takes place in the {{alveoli / alveolus}}.
Red blood cells contain {{haemoglobin / hemoglobin}}, which binds oxygen.
Most digested food is absorbed in the {{small intestine / ileum}}.

items.question: Which pigment absorbs light for photosynthesis?
Through which pores in leaves does gas exchange occur?
Which tissue transports water from the roots to the leaves?

items.explanation: This movement of sugars is called translocation.

items.question: Which gas is released as a by-product of photosynthesis?

items.text: Photosynthesis takes place in the {{chloroplasts / chloroplast}}.
The loss of water vapour from leaves is called {{transpiration}}.

items.question: What is an organism that makes its own food called?
Roughly what percentage of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
items.explanation: The rest is lost mainly as heat from respiration.

items.question: What is the role and position of a species in its ecosystem called?

items.text: Producers are eaten by {{primary consumers}}.
All the populations of different species living in one area form a {{community}}.
Organisms that break down dead material are called {{decomposers / saprotrophs}}.

items.question: What is the variable you deliberately change in an experiment called?
What is the variable you measure in an experiment called?
Which statistic shows how spread out data are around the mean?

items.text: Variables kept the same throughout an experiment are called {{control variables / controlled variables}}.
Repeating trials and calculating a mean improves the {{reliability}} of the results.
